meta.name: eu-web-compliance security headers baseline

sources.ANSSI WEB: ANSSI-PA-009 v2.0 (28 April 2021), sources.json id anssi-web
sources.ANSSI TLS: ANSSI TLS guide v1.2 (26 March 2020), sources.json id anssi-tls
sources.OWASP: OWASP Top 10:2025 category, sources.json id owasp-top10-2025
sources.best practice: No official source; never reported as a breach of a rule

meta.not_normative: ANSSI recommendations are not normative. Findings are reported against the skill's baseline, not as legal non-conformities.

required_values.https-only: Responses served over HTTPS. On a plain-HTTP local test server, check that the configuration declares the header and report it as 'declared, not effective over HTTP'.
required_values.when-html: Responses whose Content-Type starts with text/html.
required_values.recommended: Absence is reported at the severity given, never as a failure of the baseline.

check_types.present: The header exists (any value). Repeated headers are joined with ', ' before other checks, except Set-Cookie.
check_types.equals: Value, trimmed, equals one of 'values' (case-insensitive unless 'case_sensitive': true).
check_types.matches: Value matches the regular expression 'pattern' (JavaScript syntax, flags in 'flags').
check_types.not-matches: Value does not match the regular expression 'pattern'.
check_types.not-contains: Value does not contain any of the strings in 'values' (case-insensitive).
check_types.min-number: The numeric parameter named 'parameter' (form name=value, separators ';') is present and >= 'min'.
check_types.contains-directive: For CSP: the effective policy has the directive (see csp.directive_fallback) and, if 'allowed_values' is given, every source of the directive is in that list.
check_types.csp: Run every entry of csp.required_directives (as contains-directive, plus forbidden_values) and csp.forbidden_sources on each Content-Security-Policy header.
check_types.when: A check with 'when': 'present' runs only if the header exists; absence is then not a finding.
check_types.applies: A check with 'applies': 'when-html' runs only on HTML responses.

cookie_check_semantics.applies_to: 'session' = name matches cookies.session_cookie_name_pattern (or the project's declared list); 'non-session' = the others; 'all' = every cookie.
cookie_check_semantics.attribute: Attribute names are compared case-insensitively; SameSite values are compared case-insensitively.
cookie_check_semantics.present: The attribute appears in the Set-Cookie string.
cookie_check_semantics.equals: The attribute's value is one of 'values'.
cookie_check_semantics.severity_non_session: Severity to use instead of 'severity' when the cookie is not a session cookie.

severity_levels.high: Exploitable or removes a main protection. Fix before going live.
severity_levels.medium: Weakens a protection or departs from an ANSSI recommendation. Fix in the same change when possible.
severity_levels.info: Reported for awareness as a point to review (NT), never as a non-conformity; no fix required.

not_checked: TLS protocol versions, cipher suites, key sizes and certificate details (use an external TLS test; values in references/security/anssi-values.md)
Whether HTTP redirects to HTTPS (needs a request on port 80)
Whether a CSP nonce changes on each response (fetch the same page twice and compare to check it)
Whether the CSP allowlist is minimal for the third-party services actually used
Subresource integrity attributes in HTML (an HTML check, not a header check)
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy (breaks most third-party embeds; set only when the site needs cross-origin isolation)
CORS behaviour for origins other than the one used by the checker
Headers added by a CDN or proxy that is not in front of the tested URL
meta.consumers: scripts/check-security.mjs (through scripts/lib/security-baseline.mjs) reads the primary fields: per header 'check', 'values', 'pattern', 'directive', 'min', 'csp'; 'cookies' keys required_attributes, session_cookie_patterns, session_required_attributes, samesite_allowed, session_prefix_recommended; and 'absent'. The other fields ('checks', top-level 'csp', 'cookies.checks', 'cors') describe the full baseline with per-check severities, for checkers that implement them.
meta.primary_vs_detailed: When both exist, the primary fields and the detailed fields must say the same thing. Edit both together.

headers.name: Strict-Transport-Security

checks.description: max-age of one year or more
to review: includeSubDomains is missing; add it only once every subdomain of the domain is served over HTTPS (web-baseline.md section 1), so its absence is not a non-conformity

headers.rationale: Makes the browser use HTTPS for every later visit, so a first request over plain HTTP cannot be intercepted and an invalid certificate cannot be clicked through. One year and includeSubDomains are the values of the guide's example.

headers.name: Content-Security-Policy

checks.description: Evaluated with the rules of the 'csp' block below

headers.rationale: Limits where scripts, styles, frames and connections may come from, so injected markup is not executed. Set by HTTP header so that frame-ancestors and reporting work.
headers.notes: A policy found only in a <meta http-equiv> tag is accepted as the guide's fallback (R14-) with severity medium, and frame-ancestors is then reported missing because browsers ignore it in meta. Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only alone does not count as a policy.

headers.name: X-Frame-Options

checks.description: DENY or SAMEORIGIN; ALLOW-FROM is not used

headers.rationale: Defence in depth against clickjacking for browsers that do not apply CSP frame-ancestors. Must match frame-ancestors ('none' with DENY, 'self' with SAMEORIGIN).

headers.name: Referrer-Policy

checks.description: One of the four strict values; the last valid token wins when several are listed

headers.rationale: Stops full URLs (which may hold search terms, identifiers or e-mail addresses) from leaking to other sites. The guide forbids keeping the default and forbids unsafe-url.
headers.notes: When the header lists several comma-separated policies, browsers use the last one they understand: evaluate the last token.

headers.name: Content-Type
headers.rationale: An explicit type tells the browser how it may use the resource, so a file is not interpreted as something else.

headers.name: X-Content-Type-Options
headers.rationale: Stops the browser from guessing a type other than the declared one, so an uploaded text file cannot run as a script or stylesheet. Not in the ANSSI guide; complements R6.

headers.name: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy

checks.description: same-origin; same-origin-allow-popups only on pages that open a payment or sign-in popup

headers.rationale: Isolates the page's browsing context from windows opened by or opening other sites.

headers.name: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy

checks.description: cross-origin only for resources meant to be embedded by other sites

headers.rationale: Declares which sites may embed the resource, reducing cross-origin data leaks. Mentioned but not recommended by number in the ANSSI guide.

headers.name: Permissions-Policy
headers.rationale: Turns off browser features the site does not use (camera, microphone, geolocation), limiting what injected or third-party code can do. Not supported by every browser.

csp.parsing: Split the policy on ';' into directives; the first token is the directive name (lower-case), the rest are sources. When several CSP headers are present, each one must pass: the browser enforces all of them. Keywords keep their quotes ('self', 'none', 'unsafe-inline').

required_directives.rationale: Without default-src, every type of resource not named is allowed from anywhere.
Main protection against clickjacking. Works only in the HTTP header.
Plugins are not needed and have been a script-injection path; 'none' removes them.
Not covered by default-src. An injected <base> tag would otherwise redirect every relative script URL.
Not covered by default-src. Limits where forms, including injected ones, can send data.

forbidden_sources.rationale: Allows any inline script, so injected markup runs. With a nonce or hash in the same directive, modern browsers ignore it, but the guide still forbids the keyword.
Allows any inline style; injected CSS can still exfiltrate data or disguise content.
Allows eval() and equivalent constructs, which the guide forbids (R9, R10).
Re-enables inline event handlers or style attributes; move them to external files.
A data: URL can carry a whole script, which defeats the policy.
The guide forbids data: in any directive. Lower risk outside scripts; replace inline data: images and fonts with files.
A scheme alone (https:) allows scripts from any host on that scheme, which is equivalent to a wildcard for an attacker.
Loads resources over an unprotected channel, which an attacker on the network can replace.

exemptions: 'strict-dynamic' together with a nonce or hash: host and scheme sources in script-src are ignored by browsers that support it, so 'scheme-only-script' and 'wildcard-script' are reported at severity low in that case (they serve as a fallback for old browsers).

cookies.applies: Every Set-Cookie header of every response.
cookies.session_cookie_note: The name pattern is a heuristic. The project may declare its session cookie names; a declared list replaces the pattern. samesite_allowed applies to every cookie: a cookie that truly needs SameSite=None (third-party embed) is reported, and the report states the reason it is kept.

checks.rationale: Without Secure, the cookie can travel over plain HTTP, for example after a downgrade or a redirect.
A session cookie readable by JavaScript is stolen by the first injected script.
Set it whenever JavaScript does not need the cookie; the checker cannot know whether it does.
A session cookie must declare SameSite and never use None, to limit cross-site request forgery.
Strict by default, Lax when the cookie must follow links from other sites. None must come with Secure and a stated reason.
Without Domain the cookie stays on the host that set it; with Domain it is also sent to every subdomain.
The prefix makes the browser enforce Secure, Path=/ and no Domain.

cors.rationale: Browsers refuse this combination; its presence means the server logic is wrong and may echo arbitrary origins elsewhere.

cors.condition: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is '*' on an HTML response or on a response that sets a cookie
cors.rationale: A wildcard is for public, unauthenticated data only.

cors.condition: Request sent with 'Origin: https://evil.example' receives 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example'
cors.rationale: The server echoes any origin instead of checking it against an allowlist.

absent.name: Server
absent.rationale: A version number tells an attacker which known vulnerabilities to try. Hiding it does not fix anything; it only removes a hint. The ANSSI TLS guide's nginx example sets server_tokens off for this reason.
absent.meaning: Reported when the header is present and its value matches pattern.

absent.name: X-Powered-By
absent.rationale: Discloses the framework and often its version.
absent.meaning: Reported when the header is present.

absent.name: X-AspNet-Version
absent.meaning: Reported when the header is present.

absent.name: X-AspNetMvc-Version
absent.meaning: Reported when the header is present.

absent.name: X-Generator
absent.rationale: CMS generators often announce their version.
absent.meaning: Reported when the header is present and its value matches pattern.

absent.name: X-XSS-Protection
absent.rationale: The legacy browser XSS filter is retired and added vulnerabilities; the guide says to send 0 when a strict CSP is in place. Absence is fine.
absent.meaning: Reported when the header is present with a value other than 0. Absence is fine.
